title: Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning
blurb: Learned to play dozens of Atari games from pixels with a single Q-learning agent, stabilised by experience replay and a periodically updated target network.
intro: DQN is Q-learning with a convolutional network as the Q-function. Two additions make the combination stable: transitions are stored in a replay buffer and sampled at random, and the bootstrapped targets come from a frozen copy of the network that is refreshed only occasionally. The steps build tabular Q-learning, $\epsilon$-greedy exploration, the replay buffer, the target-network loss and the later Double, Dueling and prioritised-replay improvements; the capstone runs the whole training loop on a chain environment.
